extracted.intended_audience: TeX/pgf/tikz developers, driver implementers, and advanced users writing optimized frontends or drivers
extracted.subtask_description: Low-level reference for the pgf ‘system layer’ commands (\pgfsys@... and quick pgf commands) used by drivers and frontends; documents required behavior, constraints, and implementation notes for each command or family of commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use quick commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick commands execute faster than normal pgf commands and should be used only if you have very many commands to process or commands executed very often.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick commands are faster but offer less functionality; use them for performance-critical code only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick commands limitations (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick path commands do not keep track of bounding boxes, do not allow arcing corners, and do not apply coordinate transformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They do use the soft-path subsystem allowing mixing with normal path commands. Be aware of the functional trade-offs before switching to quick variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfqpoint argument restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfqpoint takes simple dimensions only (e.g., 1pt, 1cm); complex expressions like 2ex or 2cm+1pt are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only raw TeX dimensions for x and y when using quick coordinate construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathqmoveto behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Starts a path or new part of a path at coordinate (x,y) given as simple dimensions; coordinate is not transformed by the current coordinate transformation matrix, although low-level transformations still apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need a fast moveto unaffected by the CTM; suitable for performance-sensitive code where CTM should be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathqlineto behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick line-to operation that continues the current path to the given coordinate; coordinates are simple dimensions and not transformed by CTM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster than normal \pgfpathlineto but lacks bounding-box updates, corner arcing, and CTM application.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathqcurveto behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick cubic Bézier curve: three pairs of simple-dimension coordinates (s1x,s1y),(s2x,s2y),(tx,ty); control points and target specified similarly to normal curveto but without CTM and other higher-level features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for fast curve construction; remember support points and target are simple dimensions and curve is not processed for bounding boxes or corner arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfpathqcircle behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds a circle of given radius around the origin; much faster than \pgfcircle with \pgfpointorigin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need many small circles and can accept the quick command's limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick path usage limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick path usage commands (\pgfusepathq...) do not add arrows, do not modify the path (ends not shortened), and corners are not replaced by arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are intended for contexts like arrow tip definitions where arrows must not be added or path modification is undesired.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfusepathqstroke / \pgfusepathqfill / \pgfusepathqfillstroke / \pgfusepathqclip
rubrics_metrics.description: Quick versions of path usage commands: stroke/fill/fill-then-stroke/clip the current path without further processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They perform the action 'without further ado' meaning no arrow drawing, no corner/arcing, no end shortening; use where raw stroke/fill/clip is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfqbox behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserts a TeX box into a pgfpicture by escaping to TeX and inserting the box at the origin, then returning to picture typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to place typeset content into pictures; use \pgfqboxsynced when CTM sync and hyperlink placement matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfqboxsynced behavior and hyperlink note
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfqboxsynced applies the current coordinate transformation matrix to the canvas transformation matrix before inserting the box and uses TeX translations (\hskip/\raise) for translation parts so hyperlinks are placed correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale/rotation still do not apply to hyperlinks; use this when hyperlinks inside boxes must maintain correct placement under translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: System layer abstraction rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher layers should not use \special directly or check \pdfoutput; all drawing requests must be channeled through the system commands (\pgfsys@...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Driver files implement the system commands and the higher layers call those; do not bypass the system layer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Driver files and \pgfsysdriver
rubrics_metrics.description: The system layer provides default implementations; actual backend implementations live in pgfsys-xxxx.sty files and selection is via \pgfsysdriver (set by pgf.cfg).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pgf.cfg should set \pgfsysdriver appropriately; drivers should not change it if already set.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@beginpicture / \pgfsys@endpicture contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Every stream of system commands starts with \pgfsys@beginpicture and ends with \pgfsys@endpicture; these commands allow drivers to perform necessary setup/teardown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most drivers must implement these; they mark beginning/end of a pgfpicture stream.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@typesetpicturebox behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Called after a pgfpicture has been typeset with the picture box number; should insert and appropriately resize/shift the raw box according to baseline shift and box size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has a default implementation and need not be implemented by every driver, but drivers can override for custom behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pure picture variants (\pgfsys@beginpurepicture / \pgfsys@endpurepicture)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants for pictures that do not contain escaped boxes; drivers may provide more compact implementations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default implementations exist; use when picture is guaranteed 'pure' to allow optimizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@hbox / \pgfsys@hboxsynced semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands to insert a TeX (horizontal) box inside a pgfpicture; synced version applies coordinate transformation syncing with canvas transformation matrix before insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most drivers must (re-)implement these; \pgfsys@hboxsynced differs in how it treats the CTM and hyperlink preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@moveto / \pgfsys@lineto coordinate units rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinates are given as TeX dimensions and it's the driver's job to convert them to backend coordinate system (e.g., multiples of 1/72in).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use helper functions like \pgf@sys@bp for conversion; examples included in the reference illustrate usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@curveto signature and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Curveto takes six dimension arguments (x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3) to append a Bézier curve using those control and target points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocolling applies; examples show approximations of arcs using curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@rect fast-rectangle behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Appends a rectangle to the current path with lower-left corner and width/height in big points; included for speed (pdf has quick version).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be mapped back to moveto/lineto but drivers may implement faster primitives.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@closepath vs explicit lineto-to-start
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@closepath joins current point with last \pgfsys@moveto point smoothly; explicit lineto back to origin overlays lines and yields wrong corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer \pgfsys@closepath to ensure joins are rendered correctly (sharp pointed corner rather than overlapping lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canvas transformation commands (\pgfsys@transformcm / \pgfsys@transformshift / \pgfsys@transformxyscale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands to perform CTM concatenation, origin translation, and x/y scaling respectively; transformcm uses dimensionless a..d and dimensions e/f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: transformxyscale affects everything including line widths (scaling may change line appearance); transformshift has default implementation often sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@stroke graphic state dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Stroking is influenced by line width, stroke color, cap, join, dash pattern, and clipping area; a line width of 0 is the thinnest but may be invisible; 0.4pt is a good default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drivers must honor these graphic state parameters; clipping and clipping-after-stroke semantics are described with \pgfsys@clipnext.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@closestroke behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Should have same effect as closing the current path and then stroking it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default implementation exists; drivers may need not implement separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@fill behavior and interior rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Fills area bounded by current path (closing it first); nonzero winding number rule used except when \ifpgfsys@eorule is true (then even-odd rule).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filling influenced by fill color and clipping area; \pgfsys@clipnext combined with fill can make path be used for clipping as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@fillstroke semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: First fills then strokes the path; if fill and stroke colors are same, result approximates fill but stroked area slightly larger because of line thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also participates in clipping when used with \pgfsys@clipnext.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@discardpath and \pgfsys@clipnext contract
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@discardpath typically throws away current path unless preceded by \pgfsys@clipnext; \pgfsys@clipnext causes the next use of stroke/fill/discard to also set clipping to the used path (intersecting with existing clipping).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \pgfsys@clipnext after path construction but before the next stroke/fill/discard to make path contribute to clipping. Winding rule for clipping follows \ifpgfsys@eorule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic state option commands (linewidth, caps, joins, miter limit, dash)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands such as \pgfsys@setlinewidth, \pgfsys@buttcap, \pgfsys@roundcap, \pgfsys@rectcap, \pgfsys@miterjoin, \pgfsys@roundjoin, \pgfsys@beveljoin, \pgfsys@setmiterlimit, and \pgfsys@setdash set the corresponding graphic state parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \pgfsys@setdash takes a comma-separated list of dimension lengths for on/off pattern and a phase dimension; odd-length lists repeat last entry. Example: \pgfsys@setdash{3pt,3pt}{0pt}.

rubrics_metrics.name: \ifpgfsys@eorule flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines whether even-odd rule is used for filling and clipping (if set) or nonzero winding number rule (if not set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drivers must implement fill/clip according to this flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stroke/fill opacity commands
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@stroke@opacity and \pgfsys@fill@opacity set the respective opacities for stroking and filling operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drivers should implement opacity support where backend allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate stroking and filling colors
rubrics_metrics.description: pgf supports separate colors for stroking and filling via \pgfsys@color@... commands (rgb, cmyk, gray variants and @stroke/@fill variants), unlike the color package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drivers must ensure stroking and filling colors can differ; pdf backends map easily, PostScript may store colors in special variables to set them appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@color@reset behavior and optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Called when \color is used to purge internal stroking/filling color settings; default assumes color commands came 'in order' which allows optimizations. Incorrect usage (e.g., inside a box constructed earlier) can break reset semantics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If \pgfsys@color@reset@inorder is true (default), driver may assume earlier color commands occurred before the reset and optimize output; drivers can disable optimized resetting by setting the false variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@color@unstacked obscure command
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the current color to a named LaTeX color without changing the color stack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to 'trick' the color stack in special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern commands (declare and set)
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@declarepattern declares a pattern (colored or uncolored) with name, bounding box, tiling step, code and flag; \pgfsys@setpatternuncolored and \pgfsys@setpatterncolored set fill color to previously declared patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncolored patterns (flag=0) require a color at set time; colored patterns (flag=1) carry inherent color. The declared code is the drawing operations for one tile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping commands save/restore graphics state
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@beginscope saves the current graphic state; \pgfsys@endscope restores it. Changes to graphic state parameters used by stroke/fill are local to the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not call \pgfsys@beginscope while a path is non-empty (path may or may not be part of graphic state depending on backend); calling \pgfsys@discardpath prior is recommended. These commands are protocoled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image inclusion hooks and macros (imagesuffixlist / \pgfsys@defineimage)
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@imagesuffixlist lists file suffixes to try; \pgfsys@defineimage is invoked to define an image and is provided with macros like \pgf@filename, \pgf@imagewidth, \pgf@imageheight; it must set \pgf@image as the 'return value' macro to typeset the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If height/width absent, use natural size; if one present preserve aspect ratio; pdf-specific macros include \pgf@imagepage, \pgf@imagemask and \pgf@imageinterpolate.

rubrics_metrics.name: \pgfsys@definemask behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@definemask declares a mask for images, using macros like \pgf@filename and \pgf@maskmatte and must set \pgf@mask to a pdf object count usable as a soft mask.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drivers must map mask semantics to backend mask mechanisms (pdf soft mask semantics described).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading declarations (horishading / vertshading / radialshading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare horizontal, vertical, or radial shadings by name and parameters; command should create a macro \@pgfshading<name>! that when invoked inserts a shading box of declared size/specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horizontal shading: name, height, specification; vertical: name, width; radial: name, starting point and specification. Implementations must honor shading specifications and sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusable object definition and use (\pgfsys@defobject / \pgfsys@useobject)
rubrics_metrics.description: \pgfsys@defobject declares a reusable object with name, bounding box, and code; \pgfsys@useobject renders it and can run extra code (typically transformation) before rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects can be precached for performance (e.g., arrow head); code should be simple; default implementations exist but drivers may optimize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invisibility blocks (\pgfsys@begininvisible / \pgfsys@endinvisible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppress all drawing/stroking/text rendering between begininvisible and endinvisible (no paths, images, shadings), without opening TeX or graphic state groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to suppress output orthogonally to other scopes. Default implementations exist; commands are protocoled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position tracking (\pgfsys@markposition / \pgfsys@getposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-stage position tracking: \pgfsys@markposition marks a position to be saved on page shipout; \pgfsys@getposition retrieves the marked position on a later run, redefining a macro to either \relax (if unknown) or a \pgfpoint{...}{...} command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for absolute page positioning; to find page origin use special name 'pgfpageorigin' and shift positions accordingly. Drivers should implement writing/reading of positions across runs as backend allows.
